strategies.name: Suspicious Database Access and Dump Activity Across Environments (T1213.006)

analytics.name: Analytic 0676
analytics.guidance: Unusual database command-line access (e.g., `psql`, `mysql`, `mongo`) from non-admin users, occurring outside typical automation windows or without known service context. Often followed by data dumps to .sql/.csv files or outbound data transfers. Defender sees CLI tools launched interactively or by unusual parent processes, file writes to dump-like filenames, and external connections shortly after.

tuning.description: List of user or automation accounts expected to use database clients
Filename patterns used to identify data dumps (e.g., *.sql, backup_*.csv)
Time threshold for correlating execution, file write, and outbound transfer

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve: Execution of CLI tools like psql, mysql, mongo, sqlite3

log_sources.name: auditd:PATH
log_sources.channel: Creation of files with extensions .sql, .csv, .sqlite, especially in user directories

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: http::post: Outbound HTTP POST from host shortly after DB export activity

analytics.name: Analytic 0677
analytics.guidance: Database client execution (e.g., sqlcmd.exe, isql.exe) by users or from locations not tied to enterprise automation or backups. Often followed by creation of .sql/.bak/.csv files, registry artifacts for ODBC/JDBC drivers, or encrypted ZIPs. Defender sees SQL tools launched by explorer.exe, Powershell, or odd parent processes, plus file writes in user temp locations.

tuning.description: Directories where legitimate database tools are installed
List of file extensions commonly used for DB exports
Threshold for outbound data volume that may suggest large DB dumps

analytics.name: Analytic 0678
analytics.guidance: Execution of Java-based or CLI database tools (e.g., DBeaver, Beekeeper, mysql, psql) from user profiles not tied to dev/admin roles, especially when followed by file writes and cloud sync activity. Defender correlates GUI tool launches, file write events in ~/Downloads or ~/Documents, and outbound API calls to known cloud services.

tuning.description: FQDNs of sync services used to detect likely outbound DB leakages
Whether to treat low-privilege users accessing DB tools as higher risk

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Process start of Java or native DB client tools

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Writes of .sql/.csv/.xlsx files to user documents/downloads

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: HTTPS API requests to Dropbox, iCloud, Google Drive, OneDrive shortly after DB tool usage

analytics.name: Analytic 0679
analytics.guidance: Database enumeration and export activity (e.g., `SELECT * FROM`, `SHOW DATABASES`) issued via ephemeral VMs, admin APIs, or cloud shell from non-monitoring accounts. Defender correlates audit logs (CloudTrail, GCP Admin, AzureDiagnostics), storage write ops, and cross-region transfers by identities not tied to DB operations.

tuning.description: Define which IAM roles/accounts are allowed DB operations
Size threshold (MB) or file pattern for S3-based exfil monitoring
Number of rows/columns or duration to flag long-running queries

log_sources.name: AWS:CloudTrail
log_sources.channel: rds:ExecuteStatement: Large data access via RDS or Aurora with unknown session context

log_sources.name: AWS:CloudTrail
log_sources.channel: PutObject: S3 writes with .sql/.csv extension by same identity or within 5 min of DB access

log_sources.name: AWS:VPCFlowLogs
log_sources.channel: Large transfer volume (>20MB) from RDS IP range to external public IPs

analytics.name: Analytic 0680
analytics.guidance: Unusual or excessive database/table exports from SaaS database platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Firebase, BigQuery, Airtable) by users or apps not in known analytics or dev groups. Defender observes access patterns outside baseline working hours or with new query templates, and correlates those with audit logs or file downloads.

tuning.description: Query hash or shape for common BI/ETL jobs to reduce false positives
Window to define after-hours activity thresholds for DB access

log_sources.name: saas:Snowflake
log_sources.channel: QUERY: Large or repeated SELECT * queries to sensitive tables

log_sources.name: m365:unified
log_sources.channel: Bulk downloads or API extractions from Microsoft-hosted data repositories (e.g., Dynamics 365)
